Resolutions of 1973

20 resolutions, 35% unanimous. Decolonisation.

  • 325 (1973) Request of Panama to hold meetings of the Security Council in Panama City, 15-21 March 1973
  • 326 (1973) Acts of provocation by Southern Rhodesia against Zambia
  • 327 (1973) Zambia's decision to impose sanctions against Southern Rhodesia
  • 328 (1973) Urging the United Kingdom to convene a national constitutional conference with genuine representatives of the people of Zimbabwe
  • 329 (1973) Zambia's decision to impose sanctions against Southern Rhodesia and economic assistance to Zambia
  • 330 (1973) Peace and security in Latin America
  • 331 (1973) Submitting a report on the situation in the Middle East and asking for a meeting on the subject
  • 332 (1973) Military attacks conducted by Israel against Lebanon
  • 333 (1973) Calling upon States to enact and enforce legislation providing for penalties for the evasion or breach of sanctions against Southern Rhodesia
  • 334 (1973) Extension of the stationing in Cyprus of the UN Peace-keeping Force
  • 335 (1973) Admission of the Federal Republic of Germany and the German Democratic Republic to membership in the United Nations
  • 336 (1973) Admission of the Bahamas to membership in the United Nations
  • 337 (1973) Seizure of a Lebanese airliner by Israeli air forces
  • 338 (1973) A cease-fire in the Middle East
  • 339 (1973) A cease-fire between Egypt and Israel
  • 340 (1973) A UN Emergency Force for the Middle East
  • 341 (1973) Establishment of the United Nations Emergency Force
  • 342 (1973) Deciding to discontinue efforts on the basis of resolution 309 (1972) on the Namibia question
  • 343 (1973) Extension of the stationing in Cyprus of the UN Peace-keeping Force
  • 344 (1973) A peace conference on the Middle East

Security Council Record is an independent record of every resolution, vote and veto of the United Nations Security Council since 1946. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by the United Nations. For official documents, use the Security Council website and the UN Digital Library.
